why: Handler is a mock implementation (mockCostData is hard-coded in tools.ts); billingAccountName/startDate/endDate/projectId/serviceId/groupBy are only interpolated into fabricated markdown, no live Billing API call exists in this handler.
Handler returns hard-coded mockRecommendations; billingAccountName/projectId/minSavingsAmount/priority only filter/format that static array, never reaching a real sink.
currentCosts/historicalCosts are hard-coded mock arrays in the handler; billingAccountName/lookbackDays/thresholdPercentage/projectId only feed local math and markdown formatting, no external call.
billingAccountName is passed as-is to billingClient.getBillingAccount({name}), a single opaque resource-name argument to the Cloud Billing API scoped by the service account's own IAM grants.
projectId only builds the resource name `projects/${id}` passed to getProjectBillingInfo(); sink is the caller's own GCP project billing info, gated by IAM.

filter/pageToken/pageSize are forwarded wholesale as the Cloud Billing List API's own filter/paging fields; that is the tool's advertised purpose and nothing else is composed around them to break out of.
billingAccountName/pageToken feed listProjectBillingInfo() directly as opaque request fields, scoped to whatever billing account the caller's credentials already have access to.
Only pageSize/pageToken (numbers/pagination tokens) reach catalogClient.listServices(); no attacker-influenced string reaches a sensitive sink.
serviceId is passed as the `parent` field to catalogClient.listSkus(), the tool's whole declared purpose (listing SKUs for a given service); nothing else composed with it.
serviceBreakdown is a hard-coded mock array; billingAccountName/projectId/timeRange are only interpolated into markdown text output, no live GCP call is made.

requiredPermissions/project only feed resourceManager.testIamPermissions(), a read-only boolean-membership check bounded by the caller's own IAM grants; result only reveals permissions the caller supplied and already holds or lacks.
project is used only to build `projects/${id}` for resourceManager.getIamPolicy(); a straight read scoped by the caller's own resourcemanager.projects.getIamPolicy permission.
Tool takes no input (empty inputSchema); output is a static, hard-coded permission-set catalogue (DEPLOYMENT_PERMISSION_SETS).

project/permissions are forwarded verbatim to testIamPermissions(), a read-only API that only reports which caller-supplied permission strings the current credentials already hold; no mutation or escalation possible.

resource is an arbitrary string forwarded to testIamPermissions(); this API is inherently a safe read-only permission oracle bounded by the service account's own grants, and enumerating it on arbitrary resource names is the tool's stated purpose.

service is only used as a lower-cased key into the fixed DEPLOYMENT_PERMISSION_SETS map (iam/types.ts:400-403); an unrecognised or prototype-like key returns null (handled) or an object lacking requiredPermissions which throws and is caught by the handler's try/catch -- at most a caught crash on malformed input, no injection or privilege effect.

filter is the tool's entire declared purpose ('Query Google Cloud Logs with custom filters ... Cloud Logging query language') forwarded verbatim to logging.getEntries(); nothing else is composed around it to subvert.

filter is AND-appended unescaped to the timestamp bound (tools.ts:135-137), so a value like `OR 1=1` could in principle defeat the time-range restriction, but the same unrestricted, any-time log access is already available from the sibling gcp-logging-query-logs tool with identical credentials, so no security boundary beyond what the caller's own other tools already grant is crossed.

searchTerm is interpolated unescaped into ~50 quoted filter clauses (e.g. jsonPayload.message:("${searchTerm}"), tools.ts:259-312); no clean concrete bypass string was found because the same substitution happens identically in all ~50 OR'd clauses, and even a successful bypass of the severity/resource restriction would only yield log access already obtainable unrestricted via the sibling gcp-logging-query-logs tool with the same credentials.

filter, when it contains an operator, is forwarded verbatim as the Monitoring API's own filter (its declared purpose includes 'full filter expression'); otherwise it is only used for a client-side substring search. No composition to bypass.
filter is the tool's sole declared purpose ('The filter to apply to metrics'), forwarded as-is to listTimeSeries(); nothing else is concatenated with it.

query only feeds regexes in metrics_lookup.ts suggestFilter() that capture strictly [a-zA-Z0-9_]+ (resource type, line 365) or [\w-]+ (label value, line 373); those charsets cannot contain the double-quote needed to break out of the quoted filter clauses being built, so no injection is possible.

sql is the tool's entire declared purpose ('The SQL query to execute') sent directly to database.run(); running caller-supplied SQL against the caller's own Spanner database, gated by the service account's own spanner.data IAM, is the advertised function, analogous to a 'run this shell command' tool actually running commands.

instanceId only selects which Spanner instance (within the caller's own project) to list databases for via spanner.instance(id).getDatabases(); a normal resource-scoping parameter, not concatenated into anything.
Tool schema only has an unused `_dummy` placeholder parameter; no caller-controlled data reaches any sink.
The only SQL executed is a hard-coded information_schema query (tools.ts:182-187) with no caller-supplied values interpolated; instanceId/databaseId merely select which database connection to use.

instanceId/databaseId/queryType/status are concatenated unescaped into a Cloud Monitoring filter (e.g. resource.labels.instance_id = "${instanceId}", query-count.ts:122-136), and an embedded quote could defeat the instance/database restriction, but both parameters are documented as optional 'if not provided will show all instances/databases' -- simply omitting them already returns the same unrestricted result, so the injection grants no capability beyond the tool's own documented contract.

The only place a table name reaches SQL (e.g. SELECT * FROM ${tableName} LIMIT 100, tools.ts:569) is a tableName variable set only by exact case-insensitive match against real table names pulled from a parameterized information_schema query (tools.ts:501-540); the free-text `query` argument itself is never interpolated into SQL.

filter is the tool's declared purpose ('Filter for logs') forwarded to logging.getEntries() after only a regex substitution of relative-time tokens (tools.ts:533-578) that rewrites matched timestamp>/</="Nh/d/m" substrings; the caller-controlled filter is the whole intended input, matching the raw-filter contract.

traceId is validated against ^[a-f0-9]+$ before use (tools.ts:42-48) so it cannot break out of the URL path; projectId is unvalidated but only selects which GCP project's Cloud Trace API to query against a fixed host string, so no cross-host SSRF is possible and access is still gated by the caller's own bearer token.
filter is the tool's own declared 'Optional filter for traces' passed through unmodified as a single query-string value to the Cloud Trace API; startTime only feeds date arithmetic, never a sink.

Extracted traceId is regex-validated as hex (tools.ts:796, same check as gcp-trace-get-trace); the filter/logFilter values actually used are hard-coded literals ('status.code != 0', 'severity>=X') chosen from a fixed keyword list, or the same pass-through pattern as gcp-trace-list-traces -- no free-text interpolation into a restrictive clause occurs.
Tool takes no input parameters at all; it only reads and echoes the already-stored current project ID and recent-project history.

project_id is stored via stateManager.setCurrentProjectId() into a fixed local state file/env var and used to scope subsequent GCP API calls; switching the working GCP project is the tool's advertised purpose, and access to any given project remains gated by the service account's own IAM, not by this tool.
